gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
gaps.explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'I can't find my passport anywhere,' she moaned. She moaned that she ___ find her passport anywhere.
gaps.explanation: Negative can backshifts to couldn't in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm about to leave,' he said at six. At six he said he ___ about to leave.
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' backshifts like any present form: am about to → was about to.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.
